items.title: The concatenation of transport plans collapses exactly when one kernel is constant on each atom interval
items.author: Nicolas Juillet
items.work: A simultaneous Markovization of quantile processes
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 1922-1938, original Lemma 4.18: for a measure with quantile function g and atoms b_i with the intervals A_i they merge, the concatenation of the coupling with the two transport plans equals the plain composition exactly when on each A_i at least one of the two kernel functions is constant, and under that same hypothesis an identity holds for the compositions with measurable maps. The proof (source lines 1940-1967) is a disintegration computation that the statement hides entirely: the concatenation is rewritten through its numbered expression, the difference of the two plans is reduced to a sum of integrals over the atom intervals, and the sign of each summand is decided by the integral inequality for increasing functions, which is also what converts the equality case into the constancy condition; the second assertion repeats the computation under that condition.
